title: Curves are not angled properly for the majority of ornaments or for larger ones
text:
Curves are not angled properly for the majority of ornaments or for larger ones. This is a beautiful ornament stand. BUT...the only way it can actually hold an ornament is if the ornament itself has a very SHORT hanger. In other words, all the beautiful ornaments with fabric ribbons and such won't work. I tried four different ornaments, and every one of them hung way too low and touched the bottom curve of the stand. If I cut the ribbon shorter, it would not ever be able to be hung on a tree, to be able to alternate decorations.

It needs to have the top where it curls over be extended/uncurled one turn. We experimented with ours, figuring since it wasn't working anyway, the worst we could do would be to break it. Either way, we weren't able to hang ornaments on it. So my husband started tweaking the curves and coils with tools. We managed to uncurl the top enough to raise it up, which helped a little bit, but not enough. We also played with the curve in the middle, having to UNcurl it some to get a little more height. Once that was done, the ornaments still faced sideways, due to the placement of the top curl. So yet again, we played with that, and turned the top curl 90 degrees out, which finally allowed a regular ornament to be put on there without touching any of the stand or facing the back of the stand.

So, over all, it is a sturdy stand, and the bottom curl is beautiful. Note that it has a fairly large "footprint", and will take up some room. But the design is a little flawed in reality, with the curves' angles needing to be revamped to make it useful. You'll note in the photo that the ornament they display is actually very small, and does not have a drop-down hanger of any kind - it is a very short little hanger too. Most ornaments that you would display won't be like that. This would be great for small ornaments, but the larger ones that you might hang on your tree just won't work.
